items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-28
items.q: I was playing a George Deltzist on Ramport Street, Tom Anderson's son-in-law.

ctx.x: I've seen my hard board right up there. Oh, I've seen it on the biggest one. I want to use that tape, you know, that real, uh, the magnetic tape on.

Keep it in a folder. Those things are hard to find. Yeah. Yeah, Bill George was a very fair fella. Well, he's a guy, he was right in the line. He used to get all those jobs. He's the one sent for, uh, sent for, uh, George Barquet down here. When they went on the Orpins like it. I got an history up there. I believe he used Teppard too, didn't he, on that? That's right. He had an intervention on Carmel. I got there. I got them all up there. And that's why. Did you go to Chicago? For me? Yeah, I went to Chicago in…
For more information, visit www.fema.org Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: Mr. Tom Anderson sent for me... I played there... about eight or nine months.

ctx.x: Is that existing today or the high of the world? No, it's not.

Oh, no. Oh, no. So, from Jack Kerris, we were playing once, an advertisement on a Sunday, for a dance over in Gretna, while we'd play mostly every Sunday night, called the Come Clean. We'd make an advertisement on Sunday. On the wagon. On Monday. Yeah, on the wagon. So, I remember one Sunday, on the corner of 8th and Howard, a gentleman called me out the wagon. Which, he lived on 8th Street. It was a row. And he lived in one of the rows. His name was Ike Jackson. Bass violin player. Oh, he played for Tom Anderson…
What is the last name? Mac?

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you remember the first time you all played together? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Tom Anderson.

ctx.x: Do you remember the first time you all played together? About when it was, or where? Where's it?
Tom Anderson. Was it Tom Anderson? Right across from 25th? Tom Anderson? Yeah.
